reason: v2.1's pseudobinary fix assumed that hosts with (Sb + Bi) below 1/3 of the cations would fall through to this rule, but Sb and Bi were not on its sites. They are now an optional cation-site substituent (site pn), pooled with site A for the cations:anions ratio and required to be strictly below 1/3 of the cations, the exact complement of the pseudobinary rule's at-least-1/3. The majority among Ge, Pb and Sn still decides.

Same fix as gete_type: Sb and Bi are an optional cation-site substituent (site pn), pooled with site A in the cations:anions ratio and strictly below 1/3 of the cations. A host with Sn as its majority cation and Se or S as anion and no Sb or Bi is still snse_type; with Sb or Bi it can now match here, because snse_type is unchanged.
